examples.explanation: The last three hours use 3 units in total. No longer stretch stays within 4.
The two middle hours use 2 units. Any stretch including a 4 is over budget.

approaches.name: sliding window with a running total

steps.title: Clarify the input
steps.description: Asks what to return for an empty list or when even a single hour is over budget, and whether a total equal to the budget is allowed.
look_for: asks what happens if no hour fits
asks whether equal to the budget counts
hints: Before you code, is there anything about the input you'd want to pin down?
What should happen if there are no hours at all, or every hour on its own is over budget?
Settle the empty list, the nothing-fits case and the equal-to-budget case before you start.

steps.title: Grow the window to the right
steps.description: Adds each new hour to a running total of the current stretch.
look_for: moves a right edge forward one hour at a time
hints: Look at how you track the total of the current stretch.
Do you need to re-add the whole stretch every time, or can you keep a running total?
Use a sliding window: add each new hour to a running total as the right edge moves.

steps.title: Shrink from the left while over budget
steps.description: Removes hours from the left, in a loop, until the total is back within budget.
look_for: uses a while loop to shrink
subtracts the leftmost hour and moves the left edge
hints: Check what your code does when one new hour pushes the total far over budget.
Is removing a single hour from the left always enough to get back under budget?
Keep removing hours from the left in a loop until the total is within budget.

steps.title: Record the best after shrinking
steps.description: Updates the best length only once the window is valid, which can be an empty window.
look_for: updates the best length after the shrink loop
hints: Look at where you update the best length.
Could your best length ever come from a stretch that's still over budget, or start too high?
Update the best only after shrinking, and start it at 0 so 'nothing fits' gives 0.

edge_cases.description: every single hour is over budget
zero usage with a zero budget
a total exactly equal to the budget
the best stretch is at the very end

common_mistakes.description: starts the best length at 1, assuming at least one hour fits
common_mistakes.symptom: returns 1 instead of 0 for [9, 8, 7] with budget 5, and for an empty list

common_mistakes.description: shrinks with an if instead of a loop
common_mistakes.symptom: the window can stay over budget, so the answer is too long

common_mistakes.description: records the best length before shrinking
common_mistakes.symptom: counts stretches that are over budget

wrap_up_questions: What are the time and space complexity?
What changes if some hours could have negative usage, like a solar panel charging the battery?

origin_note: Original. Pattern: sliding window with a running total.
